stem:
$\text{Ni}^{2+}$ ions form a number of different complex ions, including $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$, $[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ and $[\text{Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$.

The abbreviation $en$ represents 1,2-diaminoethane. The numerical values of two stability constants, $K_{\text{stab}}$, are given in Table 5.1.

Table 5.1

| complex | $K_{\text{stab}}$ |
| :--- | :--- |
| $[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ | $4.8 \times 10^7$ |
| $[\text{Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$ | $2.0 \times 10^{18}$ |

parts.stem: A solution of $[\text{Ni}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}$ is added to a solution that contains $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NH}_3$ and $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $en$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Predict which complex ion, $[\text{Ni}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$ or $[\text{Ni}(en)_3]^{2+}$, is present in the resulting mixture in the highest concentration. Explain your answer.
